extracted.intended_audience: authors/researchers preparing and submitting papers to arXiv
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and requirements for preparing and submitting a paper to arXiv, covering accepted file formats, figure formats and sizing, version/replacement policy, timing/availability, and author responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered authors only
rubrics_metrics.description: We only accept submissions from registered authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitters must have an arXiv registration; authors themselves should make their own submissions rather than relying on third parties (e.g., secretaries).

rubrics_metrics.name: No omitted material / no abstract-only submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not submit papers with omitted figures, tables or sections. 'Abstract only' submissions are not accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such submissions are unhelpful to readers and of very limited archival value; providing links to omitted figures on other servers does not make an omission acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted text formats (order of preference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must be in one of: (La)TeX, AMS(La)TeX, PDFLaTeX; DOCX (Word 2007); PDF; PostScript; HTML with JPEG/PNG/GIF images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list is ordered by preference. The goal is to store papers in portable, stable formats; TeX/LaTeX is currently the best choice because it is an open format that does not hide information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit DVI/PS/PDF generated from LaTeX source
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv will not accept dvi, PS, or PDF created from TeX/LaTeX source in certain contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although PostScript and PDF are listed among accepted formats, arXiv prefers original source (e.g., LaTeX) rather than derivative DVI/PS/PDF produced from that source for reasons including portability and preservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word processor and scanned-document policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Users of older word processors (e.g., Microsoft Word versions prior to Word 2007) should save documents as PDF and submit that.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scanned documents are not accepted regardless of format—do not submit scans of printed pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted figure file formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures may be submitted in PS/EPS (line drawings, plots), JPEG (photographs), GIF or PNG (non-photographic bitmaps), and PDF figures (only with PDFLaTeX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the format appropriate to the figure type (e.g., EPS for line art, JPEG for photos). PDF figure support is restricted to use with PDFLaTeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure size and network considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: If figure files are too large, readers with poor network connections will have difficulty downloading them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include large figures if needed, but make all possible efforts to reduce their size to accommodate users with slow connections (arXiv has many users with poor network connections, including in developing nations). Contact www-admin@arXiv.org if you have problems with a large submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not omit figures by linking externally
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv does not accept submissions with omitted figures even if you provide a link to another server.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All content referenced in the paper should be included in the submission archive itself rather than hosted only externally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use standard LaTeX graphics packages when including figures in source
rubrics_metrics.description: If you submit figures with your (La)TeX source, use standard macro packages (e.g., graphics and graphicx) so that the figures will appear in the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: arXiv administration cannot provide TeX-related help; seek assistance from colleagues for TeX issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read arXiv response and check your submission
rubrics_metrics.description: After submission you will receive a response from arXiv; it is very important to read this response and check for errors in the copy of the abstract and the generated PostScript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The response to a successful submission includes a URL and username/password for viewing the PostScript version generated by arXiv. If you see errors or formatting problems, replace the paper to correct them or, if you cannot correct them yourself, email www-admin@arXiv.org explaining the problem before 16:00 US Eastern time and include the archive and paper number. Do not send files to that address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement policy versus new submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not make a new submission for a corrected paper or for an erratum; replace the original submission instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacing before 16:00 US Eastern time Monday through Friday will not generate an additional date stamp; authors are encouraged to update and correct papers via replacement rather than new submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author responsibility / no third-party submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must make their own submissions; third-party submissions (e.g., by secretaries) are discouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party submissions are often the ones that cause the most problems, presumably due to lack of self-interest and related factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require institutional affiliation and report numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional affiliation for the author(s) must be provided. Official report number(s) from the author(s) institution(s) must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include these metadata when submitting so the submission record is complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of official versions
rubrics_metrics.description: All official versions of submitted papers are made publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should be aware that versions placed on arXiv will be publicly accessible; see the submission version availability discussion for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability schedule and timing (daily schedule)
rubrics_metrics.description: All archives follow a daily availability schedule with no activity scheduled on weekends. Each day's submissions are made available after 20:00 US Eastern time Sunday through Thursday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a Monday submission before 16:00 ET to a given archive will be available after 20:00 ET that day and appear in the Tuesday morning mailing; Friday-before-16:00 submissions become available Sunday after 20:00 ET and appear in the Monday morning mailing; Friday-after-16:00 submissions become available Monday after 20:00 ET and appear in the Tuesday morning mailing.
